trial.title: Responsible Marijuana Sales Practices to Reduce the Risk of Selling to Intoxicated Customers

endpoints.measure: Refusal Rate of Sales of Marijuana to Obviously-intoxicated Customers
endpoints.time_frame: Establishments will be evaluated by PiP assessments 4 times (including baseline) over 5 years
endpoints.description: The rate at which establishments refuse to sell to obviously-intoxicated customers will be obtained via a pseudo-intoxicated patron (PiP) assessment

endpoints.measure: Refusal Rate of Sales of Alcohol to Obviously-intoxicated Customers
endpoints.time_frame: Alcohol establishments will be evaluated by PiP assessments 1 time during Year 1
endpoints.description: The rate at which establishments refuse to sell to obviously-intoxicated customers will be obtained via a pseudo-intoxicated patron (PiP) assessment

outcome.rationale: Primary endpoint likely to show modest non-significant trend based on prior TrainToTend null result. Policy addition is theoretical benefit without empirical validation. Secondary endpoint lacks direct evidence. Trial may not meet conventional efficacy thresholds given historical performance of similar interventions.

value.estimand: Difference in refusal rates between Policy+Training Intervention vs Usual Training Control at posttest assessments over 5 years, intention-to-treat

group_predictions.group_label: Usual and Customary Policy and Training (UC-PT) (Control) Condition

value.uncertainty: Prior direct evidence from same intervention (TrainToTend) showed null effect (11.6% vs 7.6%, p=0.401). Policy meeting addition is novel component with uncertain incremental benefit. Wide confidence interval reflects uncertainty about whether policy component can overcome training-alone limitations. Longitudinal design with crossover may dilute between-group effects.
value.rationale: Based on Buller 2020 direct evidence: same TrainToTend training in Oregon stores produced non-significant 4 percentage point increase in refusal rates. Current trial adds policy meeting component which may enhance deterrence per theory, but no empirical evidence confirms this additive effect. Predict modest 5% absolute increase (16% vs 11%) with low confidence given prior null result.

value.estimand: Refusal rate of alcohol sales to obviously-intoxicated customers in alcohol establishments at Year 1 PiP assessment
value.uncertainty: Secondary endpoint for alcohol establishments has limited direct evidence. Buller 2024 alcohol PiP study showed 56.5% overall sales rate (43.5% refusal) across CA/NM/WA with state variation. Oregon alcohol RBS training history and enforcement context unclear. Single timepoint assessment in Year 1 provides limited inference. No specific intervention targeting alcohol establishments described.
value.rationale: Alcohol establishment refusal rate predicted at ~48% based on Buller 2024 cross-state alcohol PiP data showing 43.5% refusal average, adjusted for Oregon's established RBS program. However, this trial's intervention focuses on marijuana stores; alcohol establishments may receive indirect/policy effects only. Low confidence due to indirect evidence transfer and unclear intervention mechanism for alcohol sellers.

analysis_trace.trial_identification: NCT06235632 is a randomized pretest-posttest partial crossover trial testing a Policy and Training (PT) intervention for recreational marijuana stores in Oregon. The intervention combines state regulator policy meetings with the TrainToTend online training program versus usual OLCC training.
analysis_trace.indication: Prevention of sales of recreational marijuana to obviously-intoxicated customers; secondary assessment of alcohol establishment sales refusal.
analysis_trace.patient_population: 229 recreational marijuana stores and personnel in greater Portland/Salem Oregon metro areas; also alcohol establishments for secondary endpoint. Inclusion: OLCC-licensed stores, age 21+, English-literate, with internet access.
analysis_trace.target_mechanism: Behavioral intervention combining policy deterrence (increasing perceived risk of penalties) with skills-based training to recognize intoxication signs and execute refusal skills. Based on deterrence theory and responsible beverage service (RBS) models.
analysis_trace.endpoint_interpretation: Primary: Refusal rate of marijuana sales to obviously-intoxicated customers measured via pseudo-intoxicated patron (PiP) assessments over 5 years. Secondary: Refusal rate of alcohol sales to obviously-intoxicated customers via PiP in Year 1.
analysis_trace.safety_analysis: Behavioral intervention with minimal safety risks. No adverse events anticipated from training. Potential implementation challenges include store personnel turnover and management support.
analysis_trace.key_risks: 1) Prior trial (Buller 2020) showed no significant effect of TrainToTend on intoxicated customer refusal rates (11.6% vs 7.6%, p=0.401). 2) Baseline refusal rates very low (~11%), suggesting ceiling/floor effects or lack of legal deterrence. 3) Partial crossover design dilutes between-group comparison power. 4) 5-year follow-up with PiP assessments may face store dropout and staff turnover.
analysis_trace.evidence_to_prediction: Direct evidence: Buller et al. 2020 (PMC7669561) randomized trial of TrainToTend in 146 stores across CO/OR/WA found no significant effect on refusal of sales to apparently alcohol-intoxicated customers. Intervention: 11.6% refusal; Control: 7.6%; p=0.401. This is the same training program in the same state (Oregon). Evidence role: direct_numeric (same intervention, same outcome measure, same state, similar population). However, current trial adds policy meeting component and extends to 5 years with 4 assessments.
analysis_trace.coverage_gaps: No published results for NCT06235632 specifically as of cutoff. No data on whether policy meeting addition enhances effectiveness beyond training alone. Limited generalizability from prior trial due to small sample and single timepoint assessment.

evidence_summary.citation: Buller DB, Woodall WG, Saltz R, et al. Sales to Apparently Alcohol-intoxicated Customers and Online Responsible Vendor Training in Recreational Cannabis Stores in a Randomized Trial. Int J Drug Policy. 2020;83:102860. PMCID: PMC7669561.
evidence_summary.match_assessment: Same TrainToTend intervention, same PiP outcome measure, same Oregon population, randomized design. Baseline refusal rate 11%, intervention effect non-significant.
evidence_summary.mismatch_reason: None - direct match for intervention and outcome. Minor differences: prior trial was parallel group without policy meeting component; current trial adds policy meeting and extends follow-up.

evidence_summary.citation: Buller DB, et al. Sales to Apparently Intoxicated Customers in Three States With Different Histories of Responsible Beverage Service Training. J Stud Alcohol Drugs. 2024;85(3):312-321. PMCID: PMC11095494.
evidence_summary.match_assessment: Same PiP methodology for alcohol establishments, shows RBS training can reduce overservice when combined with policy enforcement (NM/WA vs CA). Supports policy+training approach directionally but not directly applicable to marijuana.
evidence_summary.mismatch_reason: Different substance (alcohol vs marijuana), different intervention timing, different states. Provides directional support for policy+training but cannot transfer exact effect sizes.
